project.objective: Did Estefania Zambrana and her husband Antonio Beisaga of Cochabamba, Bolivia have a son named Ricardo, baptized 1874, in addition to their two known children (b. 1867 and 1877)?

questions.question: Was a child named Ricardo baptized in Cochabamba, Bolivia circa 1874, recorded as a son of Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana?
questions.rationale: The research objective asks whether the couple had a son named Ricardo baptized ca. 1874. Bolivian Catholic parish baptism registers for Cochabamba survive for this period on FamilySearch and are the primary record type for verifying a baptism event. This question targets that single event directly and is testable through those registers. No prior questions exist, so this is the first decomposition of the objective.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All plan items for q_001 are completed. The primary indexed collection (Bolivia, Catholic Church Records, 1566-2020, collection 1922463) was searched at 91-99% coverage for the target period 1868-1880 across all major Cochabamba city parishes (San Ignacio de Loyola, San José, Santo Domingo, San Antonio de Padua). A broad-net search for all children of Antonio Beisaga + Estefania Zambrana 1865-1880 returned exactly 4 children (Luis 1871, Tomaza 1875, Jerónimo 1877, Maria de la o 1878) — no Ricardo. The legacy partial index (collection 1520550) was also searched with no results. The full-text search corpus contains no coverage for Cochabamba registers in 1868-1880 ('Beisaga' alone yields 0 results in the FT index for that date range). Image browse of the 005091274 prefix volumes confirmed they are 20th-century surname indexes (1880+ era), not 1870s registers — the actual 1870s-era registers for San Ignacio de Loyola are already in the highly indexed 004016032/004016033 prefix volumes included in the collection-wide indexed search. The remaining un-indexed residual (4-9% of the 1870s registers) cannot be efficiently browsed and does not outweigh the comprehensive negative result from the indexed majority. Research is reasonably exhaustive: no additional accessible search paths have been identified.
exhaustive_declaration.stop_criteria: Five threshold questions met: (1) sufficient breadth — indexed, FT, legacy index, and image-browse strategies all executed; (2) all accessible repositories identified and searched; (3) spelling variants Beisaga/Beizaga both searched; (4) all Cochabamba parishes in collection 1922463 covered; (5) full 1865-1880 date range searched. Remaining gap — 4-9% un-indexed residual in 1870s registers — is insufficient to overturn the comprehensive indexed negative across multiple search strategies.

items.rationale: Bolivia, Catholic Church Records, 1566-2020 (collection 1922463) is the most comprehensive indexed + image collection for Bolivian parish registers and the primary search vehicle. Civil registration did not begin in Bolivia until 1940, so Catholic baptism registers are the only official vital record for a child born ca. 1874. Searching for Ricardo with parents Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana across a ±2-year window around 1874 is the highest-probability first step. Records are in Spanish. Per loc_001, this collection covers all major Cochabamba city parishes.

Bolivia, Baptisms, 1560-1938 (collection 1520550) is a separate legacy partial index assembled from a different indexing pass than collection 1922463. Although loc_001 flags it as incomplete, it was indexed independently and may surface entries where the 1922463 index has gaps or variant spellings. A negative in 1520550 cannot confirm absence, but a positive would be a lead worth verifying in the original image. Executed after pli_001 to avoid duplication; serves as a cross-check on the primary indexed search.

Full-text co-occurrence search for the two surnames 'Beisaga' and 'Zambrana' as separate required terms across the unscoped FamilySearch full-text corpus (search-full-text skill). Per record-type guide, this is the highest-yield tactic when name-indexed search stalls: it finds records where the index is wrong, the name is written in a variant form, or the full-text AI transcription captures what the indexer missed. For a compound Latin American name pattern (Paterno Materno), searching both parent surnames as a co-occurrence lands the child's baptism, the parents' own marriage, or burial records — any of which may name Ricardo. Not scoped to a specific collection ID.

Search Bolivia, Catholic Church Records (collection 1922463) for the two known children: Geronimo Beisaga (b. ca. 1867) and Fructuosa Beisaga Zambrana (b. ca. 1877). Per BCG Standard 11, starting-point facts must be verified before being relied upon. Finding these baptisms in original records: (a) confirms Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana as a documented couple in Cochabamba parish registers; (b) identifies their specific parish, narrowing the browse scope for Ricardo; (c) yields godparent names — FAN evidence — that may recur as godparents or witnesses in Ricardo's baptism if he existed; and (d) establishes the temporal pattern of the couple's children, bracketing the ca. 1874 gap where Ricardo is claimed.

Search Bolivia, Marriages, 1630-1940 (collection 1520564) and Bolivia, Catholic Church Records, 1566-2020 (collection 1922463) for the marriage of Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana. Per the record-type guide, a parentage question always requires a dedicated search for the candidate parents' marriage: it (a) confirms the couple as a documented unit; (b) supplies Estefania's maiden name 'Zambrana' in an original record, which census and death records often omit; and (c) dates the union relative to Ricardo's claimed 1874 birth, corroborating that the couple could be his parents. Note the limit: the marriage record proves they wed, not that Ricardo is their child — a child-placing record (his baptism) is still required.

Browse San Ignacio de Loyola parish volumes (image group prefix 005091277, 79-96% name-indexed; prefix 005091274, full-text searchable) via image_search for pages covering 1872-1876. San Ignacio de Loyola is the major central-city Cochabamba parish (1828-1957) and, if the family's parish is identified from pli_004, its volumes are the highest-priority target for a manual browse when indexed search returns nothing. This item serves as a browse fallback if pli_001 and pli_002 yield no result: it ensures that an entry missed by the name index but present in the image is not overlooked. Per loc_001, some San Ignacio de Loyola volumes are full-text searchable but NOT name-indexed, so record_search alone will miss them.

Top result: 'Ricardo Beisaga' (Male, score 4.19), recordId QGJC-FX3Y. Record title says 'Registro para Mariano' — Ricardo may appear as a relative in another person's record. Requires record_read to confirm parent names and relationship.

Collection 1520550 (Bolivia Baptisms legacy index). Same search parameters as pli_001. Zero results — this legacy partial index does not contain a record for Ricardo Beisaga with parents Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana for 1872-1876 in Cochabamba.

Search for Geronimo Beisaga (subject 9QTV-K8P), parents Antonio Beisaga + Estefania Zambrana, birth 1865-1869, Cochabamba. 17 results returned, all Beisaga family members, but per ranker diagnostic all matchScores < 0.01 — treat as real negative for this query. Top name matches include 'Jeronimo Beisaga' (Spanish variant) in records for Juan and Pedro — these may be Geronimo appearing as a godparent or parent-relative. Will retry with Jeronimo variant and without parent filters.

Search for Fructuosa Beisaga Zambrana (subject P89Y-ZJK), parents Antonio Beisaga + Estefania Zambrana, birth 1875-1879, Cochabamba. 12 results found. Ranks 1-2 (71DT-KTT2, 71DL-V2N2) already attached to subject P89Y-ZJK. Record titles suggest Fructuosa appears as a parent in children's baptism records, not as the baptized child herself. Will read to identify family parish.

Search for marriage of Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana in collection 1520564 (Bolivia Marriages 1630-1940), 1855-1870, Cochabamba. Zero results. Will retry in collection 1922463 which covers marriages 1566-2020.

Retry for Geronimo Beisaga with Spanish name variant 'Jeronimo'. Same 17-result pool returned. All matchScores < 0.01 per ranker diagnostic — real negative for this query. Subject 9QTV-K8P remains too thin to resolve. Jeronimo Beisaga appears in records for Juan (QGJC-X3YL) and Pedro (QY37-2MN2) as a relative, possibly as godfather/father, not as the baptized child. Indexed birth record for Geronimo/Jeronimo Beisaga with parents Antonio + Estefania not found in collection 1922463.

Retry for marriage of Antonio Beisaga + Estefania Zambrana in collection 1922463 (Bolivia Catholic Church Records 1566-2020). Top search result (score 8.31): 'Registro para Antonio Beizaga y Estefania Zambrana' (QL7X-YN65, birthDate 1845 for Antonio). Record title directly names both parties — strong candidate for their marriage or joint registration. Also: 4FC5-7B6Z ('Registro para Lauriano Torrico') already attached to subject Antonio Beisaga 9QTV-KD3. Reading both records.

record_read of QGJC-FX3Y (Ricardo Beisaga). Ricardo appears as FATHER of Mariano Beisaga Launa, baptized 3 Oct 1908 in Sicaya, Capinota, Cochabamba. Wife: Petrona Launa. This confirms a Ricardo Beisaga existed in Cochabamba, age consistent with ca. 1874 birth, but this record does not name his parents. Does not directly answer whether he is a son of Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana.

record_read of 71DT-KTT2 (Anselmo Torrico Beisaga baptism, 20 Apr 1890). Fructuosa Beisaga appears as mother, married to Laureano Torrico. Parish: Santo Domingo, Cochabamba city. This places Fructuosa in the Santo Domingo parish ca. 1890 but is not her own baptism record.

record_read of QL7X-YN65 (marriage record). CONFIRMED: Antonio Beizaga (b.1845, parents Calisto Beizaga + Manuela Rojas) married Estefania Zambrana (b.1848, parents Francisco Zambrana + Manuela Claros) on 23 Mar 1870 at San Jose parish, Cochabamba. 'Beizaga' is a spelling variant of 'Beisaga'. Collection: Bolivia, Cochabamba, Marriages, 1615-1976 (auto_M9J1-9SN).

record_read of 4FC5-7B6Z (Lauriano Torrico marriage, 30 Mar 1890). CONFIRMED: Fructuosa Beisaga (b. 1867) is daughter of Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana. Fructuosa married Laureano Torrico (b. 1860). This record explicitly names both parents of Fructuosa — direct parentage evidence. Note: tree has Fructuosa born 1877, but this record states 1867 — possible date conflict requiring resolution.

Broad child search: all children of Antonio Beisaga + Estefania Zambrana, birth 1865-1880, collection 1922463. NO Ricardo found. Children indexed: Jeronimo (QPTW-LPGT, 30 Sep 1877, San Ignacio de Loyola), Maria de la o (7DW1-HX2M, 17 Dec 1878, San Jose), Luis (W865-RRT2, 18 Aug 1871, Cochabamba Cercado), Tomaza (71W1-TCW2, 28 Dec 1875, San Ignacio de Loyola). Fathername 'Beisaga' variant.

Same broad child search with 'Beizaga' surname variant (the marriage record spelling). Same 4 children returned. No Ricardo found under either spelling variant. Absence of Ricardo in indexed collection 1922463 for 1865-1880 is significant negative evidence, but collection coverage is not 100%.

CONFIRMED: Jerónimo Beisaga Zambrana baptized 30 Sep 1877, San Ignacio de Loyola, Cochabamba. Parents: Antonio Beisaga + Estefania Zambrana. Contradicts tree date of 1867 for Geronimo — tree likely has Geronimo and Fructuosa birth years swapped. Direct parentage evidence for Jerónimo.

CONFIRMED: Luis Beisaga Zambrana baptized 18 Aug 1871, Cochabamba Cercado. Parents: Antonio Beisaga + Estefania Zambrana. Previously unknown child of Antonio and Estefania — not in tree. Fills gap between marriage (1870) and Tomaza (1875). No Ricardo between 1871 and 1875.

CONFIRMED: Tomaza Beisaga Zambrana baptized 28 Dec 1875, San Ignacio de Loyola. Parents: Antonio Beisaga + Estefania Zambrana. Previously unknown child — not in tree. Family used San Ignacio de Loyola parish for 1875 and 1877 baptisms.

CONFIRMED: Maria de la o Beisaga Zambrana baptized 17 Dec 1878, San José, Cochabamba. Parents: Antonio Beisaga + Estefania Zambrana. Previously unknown child — not in tree. Family returned to San José parish (same as their 1870 marriage) for this 1878 baptism. NO Ricardo found in any indexed child record for Antonio + Estefania in 1865-1880.

Full-text co-occurrence search: Beisaga AND Zambrana, 1860-1885. Zero results. The Cochabamba Catholic parish registers for 1860-1885 are not indexed in the FamilySearch full-text corpus for this surname combination.

Full-text co-occurrence: Beisaga AND Zambrana, all years. 3 results found, ALL from Potosi department (not Cochabamba) and dated 1907-1919 — incidental co-occurrences of unrelated Beisaga and Zambrana individuals on shared register pages. No Cochabamba entry, no Ricardo, no entry for Antonio + Estefania. Not relevant to q_001 in the target period or location.
Full-text search: Beizaga (alternate spelling) AND Zambrana, all years. Zero results. Spelling variant search confirms no FT coverage of this surname in the target context.
Full-text search: Ricardo AND Beisaga, 1860-1885. Zero results. No register page in the FT corpus for this period names both Ricardo and Beisaga.

Diagnostic: surname Beisaga alone, 1868-1880. Zero results. CRITICAL FINDING: The FamilySearch full-text corpus contains no indexed page from 1868-1880 mentioning the Beisaga surname. This confirms the Cochabamba Catholic registers (San Ignacio de Loyola, San Jose) for the target period 1870-1878 — the same registers where the family's other children ARE indexed — are not in the FT corpus for this era. Full-text cannot find Ricardo even if an entry exists; image browsing (pli_006) is the only remaining non-indexed search path.

Image browse of vol 005091274_006 (San Ignacio de Loyola / La Compañía de Jesús, Cochabamba). Header card reveals: INDICE BAUTISMOS, volumes L-M, years 1880-1957. This is a 20th-century surname index, NOT a 1870s-era baptism register. Completely outside the target period 1872-1876. No further browsing warranted for this volume.

Image browse of vol 005091274_002 (San Ignacio de Loyola). Internal index page covers surnames B-C, years 1905-1906. Confirms the 005091274 prefix volumes are alphabetical surname indexes for the 20th century, not 1870s registers. Target period 1872-1876 is NOT in these volumes.

CONCLUSION FOR PLI_006: All sampled 005091274 volumes are 20th-century surname indexes for La Compañía de Jesús / San Ignacio de Loyola, not 1870s-era baptism registers. The actual 1870-1880 registers at this parish are in the 93-99% indexed volumes (prefixes 004016032, 004016033, 004016031, 005091282) that were covered by the comprehensive indexed search (log_012, log_013). Those searches returned only 4 children of Antonio Beisaga + Estefania Zambrana (1871, 1875, 1877, 1878) with no Ricardo. Image browsing of the 005091274 volumes would not surface a Ricardo baptism from 1872-1876 since those volumes are out-of-period. Pli_006 exhausted.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Analysis: q_001

**Question:** Was a child named Ricardo baptized in Cochabamba, Bolivia circa 1874, recorded as a son of Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana?

### Sources Consulted

Seven original ecclesiastical records from FamilySearch's Bolivia Catholic Church Records 1566–2020 (collection 1922463) were retrieved and extracted:

- **S1** (src_001): Marriage register entry, San José Parish, Cochabamba — marriage of Antonio Beizaga and Estefania Zambrana, 23 March 1870. *Original source, primary information on the marriage event; secondary on the parties' parentage.* Names both parties, their parents (Calisto Beizaga + Manuela Rojas for Antonio; Francisco Zambrana + Manuela Claros for Estefania), and witnesses.

- **S2** (src_002): Marriage register entry, 30 March 1890, Cochabamba — Laureano Torrico and Fructuosa Beisaga. *Original source; secondary information identifying Fructuosa's parents as Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana.* Places Fructuosa's birth circa 1867–1870.

- **S3** (src_003): Baptism register entry, 3 October 1908, Sicaya, Capinota, Cochabamba — baptism of Mariano Beisaga Launa. *Original source, primary information on Mariano's baptism; secondary on his parents.* Names Ricardo Beisaga as father and Clementina Launa as mother. Does **not** name Ricardo's own parents or birthplace.

- **S4** (src_004): Baptism register entry, San Ignacio de Loyola Parish, Cochabamba — Jerónimo Beisaga Zambrana, baptized 30 September 1877. *Original source, primary information.* Parents: Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana.

- **S5** (src_005): Baptism register entry, San José Parish, Cochabamba — Maria de la o Beisaga Zambrana, baptized 17 December 1878. *Original source, primary information.* Parents: Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana.

- **S6** (src_006): Baptism register entry, Cochabamba Cercado — Luis Beisaga Zambrana, baptized 18 August 1871. *Original source, primary information.* Parents: Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana.

- **S7** (src_007): Baptism register entry, San Ignacio de Loyola Parish, Cochabamba — Tomaza Beisaga Zambrana, baptized 28 December 1875. *Original source, primary information.* Parents: Antonio Beisaga (Beizaga) and Estefania Zambrana.

Negative search results are documented in log entries log_001 through log_025.

### Search Strategy and Coverage

Three complementary strategies were executed:

**1. Indexed record search (primary):** FamilySearch collection 1922463 was searched at an estimated 91–99% indexed coverage for Cochabamba parishes in the 1865–1885 period. Searches used surname variants Beisaga, Beizaga, and Beysaga as both principal and parent names, across the full target date range. A broad-net search for all children of Antonio Beisaga/Beizaga and Estefania Zambrana between 1865 and 1880 returned exactly four children: Luis (1871), Tomaza (1875), Jerónimo (1877), and Maria de la o (1878). No child named Ricardo appeared. The legacy partial index (collection 1520550) was also searched with no additional results.

**2. Full-text search:** A corpus search for '+Beisaga' with the year range 1868–1880 returned zero results, confirming that Cochabamba Catholic registers for this period are absent from the FamilySearch full-text transcription corpus. This search path is unavailable.

**3. Image browse of apparently un-indexed volumes:** Volume group 005091274 carried `fulltextSearchable: true` metadata. Direct image reads of these volumes revealed they are 20th-century surname indexes (*Índice Bautismos*) covering 1880–1957 — not 1870s baptism registers. The actual 1870s–1880s registers are in the 93–99% indexed volume groups (004016032, 004016033) already covered by the indexed search. No additional un-indexed 1870s volumes were identified.

**Residual gap:** An estimated 4–9% of Cochabamba parish records for the target period remain un-indexed. Physical inspection of original registers at the Bolivian diocesan archives would be required to eliminate this gap.

### Evidence Analysis

**Established facts:**
- Antonio Beizaga and Estefania Zambrana married 23 March 1870 in Cochabamba — their union is documented by an original source with primary information (S1/src_001). *Direct evidence of the couple's existence.*
- Five children of this couple are confirmed through original records: Fructuosa (b. ~1867, documented via her 1890 marriage S2/src_002), Luis (b. 1871, S6/src_006), Tomaza (b. 1875, S7/src_007), Jerónimo (b. 1877, S4/src_004), and Maria de la o (b. 1878, S5/src_005). None is named Ricardo.
- A man named Ricardo Beisaga resided in Sicaya, Capinota, Cochabamba in 1908 as father of Mariano Beisaga Launa (S3/src_003). His estimated birth circa 1875 is plausible for a son of the couple. *Indirect evidence only — consistent with the hypothesis but not probative of parentage.*

**What is not established:**
- No record names Ricardo Beisaga as a child of Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana.
- The 1908 record (S3/src_003) names Ricardo's child, not Ricardo's own parents. It cannot establish his parentage.
- The consistency of Ricardo's name, age, and region with membership in the family is circumstantial. Consistency is not proof.

**Evidence type assessment:** The systematic negative search evidence — a multi-strategy, reasonably exhaustive survey returning no baptism for Ricardo as son of Antonio+Estefania — constitutes indirect negative evidence under the GPS. It does not absolutely exclude the possibility (4–9% residual remains), but a thorough multi-source negative at 91–99% coverage shifts the burden significantly against the hypothesis.

### Conflicts

No conflicting assertions were identified. No competing hypotheses were formally tracked.

### Conclusion

**Tier: Not Proved**

The preponderance of accessible evidence fails to establish that a child named Ricardo was baptized in Cochabamba, Bolivia circa 1874 as a son of Antonio Beisaga and Estefania Zambrana. The reasonably exhaustive search (91–99% coverage) of the primary repository produced no such baptism record. Five other children of the couple are positively documented, none named Ricardo. A Ricardo Beisaga of plausible age and location exists in 1908 records (src_003), but no source connects him to Antonio and Estefania as his parents.

A definitive resolution would require physical inspection of the approximately 4–9% of Cochabamba parish registers not yet indexed, particularly those of San José, San Ignacio de Loyola, and surrounding parishes for the years 1873–1876.

quirks: Bolivia's civil registration began only in 1940; all births in 1874 are documented exclusively in Catholic parish registers.

The city of Cochabamba had at least six active Catholic parishes (Santo Domingo 1609-1945, San Antonio de Padua 1826-1966, San Joaquín 1826-1966, Santa Ana de Cala Cala 1826-1978, San Ignacio de Loyola 1828-1957, San José 1863-1975) — a baptism could appear in any of them; search all.

Collection 1520550 (Bolivia, Baptisms, 1560-1938) is a legacy partial index and explicitly known to be incomplete — a negative result there does not mean no record exists; always verify with original images in collection 1922463.
Some San Ignacio de Loyola volumes (prefix 005091274) are full-text searchable but NOT name-indexed (0% recordSearchablePercent) — use fulltext_search rather than record_search for those volumes.
All records are in Spanish; use the FamilySearch Spanish Genealogical Word List for unfamiliar terms.
The Archive of the Archbishopric of Cochabamba (Calle Calama 169; tel. 591-4-4256563) holds duplicate and original sacramental records not fully accessible online.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Cochabamba, Bolivia (1867–1877)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** City of Cochabamba established 1571; Department of Cochabamba formed 1826 upon Bolivian independence
- **Administrative center:** City of Cochabamba, Cercado Province
- **Religion:** Roman Catholic (exclusive institutional vital-record keeper in this period)
- **Population (Bolivia national):** ca. 1,372,000–1,524,000 (1860–1874, Gapminder)

## Vital records
- Civil registration began 1940 — **not applicable** for 1874. Catholic parish registers are the only official vital-record source.

## Church records — PRIMARY SOURCE
Six parishes with digitized records on FamilySearch for the city of Cochabamba (Cercado):
- Santo Domingo (1609–1945)
- San Antonio de Padua (1826–1966)
- San Joaquín (1826–1966)
- Santa Ana de Cala Cala (1826–1978)
- San Ignacio de Loyola (1828–1957)
- San José (1863–1975)

All accessible via collection 1922463 (Bolivia, Catholic Church Records, 1566-2020) — index & images, free on FamilySearch.

## Digitization levels (city volumes from volume_search)
- San Ignacio de Loyola: 79–96% name-indexed (prefix 005091277); 0% indexed but full-text searchable (prefix 005091274)
- San Antonio de Padua: 89–95% name-indexed (prefix 005091258, 005091257)
- San Joaquín: 88–96% name-indexed (prefix 005091261, 005091262)
- Matrimonial investigations Cochabamba city 1871-1879 (005091284_001): 34% indexed

## Key collections
| Collection | ID | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Bolivia, Catholic Church Records, 1566-2020 | 1922463 | FS free, index + images |
| Bolivia, Baptisms, 1560-1938 (legacy partial index) | 1520550 | FS free, index only |
| Bolivia, Marriages, 1630-1940 | 1520564 | FS free |
| Bolivia, Deaths, 1750-1920 | 1520566 | FS free |

## Physical repository
Archive of the Archbishopric of Cochabamba, Calle Calama 169, Cochabamba (tel. 591-4-4256563); Archivo y Biblioteca Nacionales de Bolivia.

## Research tips
1. Search collection 1922463 first — most comprehensive, has images.
2. A negative in collection 1520550 does not mean no record — it is a known partial index.
3. Search all six city parishes if indexed search is negative.
4. Full-text search (not record_search) for San Ignacio de Loyola prefix 005091274 volumes.
5. All records in Spanish.
